findings.claim: The typed-turn migration requires zero-difference shadow parity against legacy even though its dependencies intentionally change legacy behavior, making the acceptance gate internally impossible or forcing implementers to preserve known defects.
findings.evidence: typed-turn-assembly/spec.md says it depends on behavior-changing changes: "Dependencies: context-history-integrity, fail-closed-tool-arguments, deterministic-prompt-assembly, progressive-skill-runtime, model-path-resiliency." Its verification then requires "tests/turn_shadow_parity.rs: in `shadow` mode, every request in the corpus reports zero hash, order, tool-eligibility, and context-count differences". But dependency specs intentionally change those exact dimensions, e.g. deterministic-prompt-assembly changes ordering via "Fixed section order" and progressive-skill-runtime changes tool eligibility via "The tool set and active skills are re-projected per step" / "Explicit activation".
findings.suggested_fix: Change shadow parity to compare against an explicit expected typed baseline or restrict zero-difference checks to unaffected corpus cases; record intentional deltas separately instead of requiring zero differences across hash, order, tool eligibility, and context counts.

findings.claim: The default-flip task is ordered inside the same change that requires shadow evidence, but the evidence can only exist after the typed path is implemented and exercised.
findings.evidence: typed-turn-assembly/verification.md puts both in one task list: "4.2 Run the parity corpus at Tier 2 and in the live smoke set; record the zero-difference evidence in the decision log" followed by "4.3 Flip default to `typed`; keep `legacy` for one minor release". The spec says "The default SHALL change to `typed` only after a recorded zero-difference result over the parity corpus", so flipping inside the same implementation change risks proceeding before external/live evidence exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the default flip into a separate follow-up spec/change gated on recorded parity and live-smoke evidence; keep this change limited to adding legacy/shadow/typed modes and producing reports.

findings.claim: The spec contradicts itself on whether `versions.toml` is in scope or an external precondition.
findings.evidence: fail-closed-tool-arguments/spec.md Scope includes "`versions.toml` (operator adds `jsonschema = \"0.49.4\"`)" and What changes says "`jsonschema` is recorded in `versions.toml` ... before this change merges." But fail-closed-tool-arguments/verification.md says under Precondition: "Operator records `jsonschema = \"0.49.4\"` in `versions.toml`; this change does not edit that file".
findings.suggested_fix: Make `versions.toml` unambiguously either an implementation task in this change or an external precondition that blocks starting/merging, and remove it from Scope if it is not edited.

findings.claim: Multiple requirements rely on Codex source citations that the packet marks as missing, so downstream implementers cannot verify the ported behavior from the packet.
findings.evidence: The artifact cites Codex paths such as "core/src/context_manager/history.rs:563-581", "context-fragments/src/fragment.rs:56-119", "core/src/session/turn_context.rs:194-246", and "codex-mcp/src/connection_manager.rs:258-259". The packet's cited_paths marks these as "MISSING core/src/context_manager/history.rs", "MISSING context-fragments/src/fragment.rs", "MISSING core/src/session/turn_context.rs", and "MISSING codex-mcp/src/connection_manager.rs".
findings.suggested_fix: Include the relevant Codex excerpts or an evidence appendix in the spec packet, or downgrade these from concrete porting claims to design requirements not dependent on unverifiable line citations.

findings.claim: Checkpoint resume is included as a requirement without any corresponding Codex comparison or gap evidence in the spec's Why section.
findings.evidence: context-history-integrity/spec.md Why discusses reducers, tool-call pairs, tokenizers, and tool output: "Two independent context reducers run back to back...", "Tool output enters history unbounded...". The What changes then adds unrelated scope: "Checkpoint resume uses `restore_state`; the endpoint no longer starts a fresh run with a prose input" and the Spec delta adds "Requirement: Checkpoint resume restores checkpoint state".
findings.suggested_fix: Add the missing assessment/analysis evidence and Codex comparison for checkpoint resume, or move checkpoint resume to its own spec delta/change if it is a separate defect.
